newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks seen up slightly on rescue fund.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks seen up slightly on rescue fund.

text.p: Thai stocks were expected to gain slightly on Monday on improved market sentiment following an announcement by the finance minister over the weekend that a stock market support fund would be set up, brokers said.

"The market has absorbed all the bad news including poor first quarter corporate earnings and concerns about the Thai baht. I think the stock market support fund would help boost the market sentiment today," said Bunsom Kesapradist of Asia Credit.
After sharp declines over the past few weeks, the composite SET index rose 3.32 points to end at 561.19 on Friday.

Finance Minister Amnuay Viravan said on Saturday that Thai commercial banks had volunteered to pool the 50 billion baht fund to help shore up the stock market which tumbled to an eight-year low last week.
The SET index has declined 15 percent so far this month and lost 32.5 percent since January.
Brokers said they expected turnover would be thin today as the market will be closed on Tuesday for a Buddhist religious holiday.
